title: QuickQuiz attempts export
description: The file written by Export my data and read by Import: the finished attempts of one user with their answers, marked questions, comments and challenged questions. Quizzes are identified by content hash (or by title), not by the instance-specific quiz id, so the file can be imported into another instance that has the same quizzes. Other platforms can write this format to bring their results in. HOW TO COMPUTE quiz.hash. The hash identifies a quiz by its content, so it is the same on every QuickQuiz instance. Start from the quiz JSON object, in the shape of quiz-questions.schema.json (title, source, timeLimitMinutes, timeLimitText, questions, ...). 1) Remove the top-level keys "attempt", "author" and "syllabus" (if present). 2) In every object of the "questions" array remove the keys "domain" and "domainGuessed" (if present). Keep the order of the questions and of the options. Change nothing else: keep every other key and value exactly as in the quiz file, including empty strings, null and false. 3) Serialise the result to canonical JSON: object keys sorted ascending by Unicode code point at every nesting level; no whitespace anywhere (separators are "," and ":" only); strings use the standard JSON escapes (\" \\ \n \r \t \b \f, other control characters below U+0020 as \u00xx with lowercase hex) and every other character, including non-ASCII such as "é" or "日本", is written as itself and NOT as a \uXXXX escape; integers without a decimal point or exponent; true, false and null in lowercase. 4) Encode that text as UTF-8. 5) Compute SHA-256 of the bytes and write it as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. In Python: hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(content, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). A worked example is in x-hashExample. If your platform cannot compute the hash, omit quiz.hash and give the exact quiz title instead: the quiz is then matched case-insensitively by title and must match exactly one quiz on the instance, otherwise the attempt is reported as missing or ambiguous and is not imported. When quiz.hash is present it is authoritative and the title is not used for matching.

format.description: Constant that identifies the file type.

version.description: Format version. Files with another version are rejected.

exportedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the export. Informational.

attempts.description: The attempts to import. Each one is processed independently.

id.description: Identifier of the attempt in the source system. Importing the same id twice for the same user imports it only once, so keep it stable between exports.

quiz.description: Which quiz the attempt belongs to. Give hash, title or both. See the schema description for how to compute the hash.

hash.description: Content hash of the quiz, 64 lowercase hex characters. Authoritative when present.

title.description: Quiz title. Used for matching only when hash is absent; also shown in the import report.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time when the attempt started. A value without a time zone is read as UTC.

finishedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time when the attempt finished. A value without a time zone is read as UTC.

finishReason.description: "submitted" when the user finished it, "expired" when the time ran out.

timeUsedSeconds.description: Seconds actually spent on the attempt.

answers.description: Chosen options per question: key is the 1-based question number as a string, value the 0-based indexes of the chosen options in the quiz file's order. Unanswered questions are left out. Single-choice questions take at most one index. The score is recomputed from these answers, never read from the file.

marked.description: 1-based numbers of the questions marked for review.

comments.description: The user's note per question, keyed by 1-based question number as a string. Blank notes are ignored. No size limit.

challenged.description: 1-based numbers of the questions whose answer the user challenges, flagged during review. Optional: a file without it imports as no challenged questions.

x-hashExample.description: Worked example for quiz.hash: the quiz as it appears in a quiz file, the canonical JSON after steps 1 to 3, and the SHA-256 after steps 4 and 5.
